why: Raises $22,000 reverses the sign; lowers $40,000 charges the 20c premium on all 200,000 current bags (ignores the tier and the extra volume); raises $40,000 ignores the tier and the delivery cost, so the 20,000 extra bags earn $2 each; no single slip (ignoring the 10% rise gives −$28,000, ignoring delivery costs +$12,000) lands on −$22,000.

$800 stops at the Standard fee, $1,184 divides the $2.024m support income evenly over the 1,710 plan accounts ignoring the 3x ratio, and $2,640 adds the $240 hosting fee to the Priority fee; leaving the hosting fee in gives $4,008 and taking it only from plan accounts gives about $3,520, so no slip lands on $2,400.

$9.7m is the new total margin (81 × 120,000) instead of the increase, $360,000 is the answer a factor of 10 out, and $970,000 is the new total a factor of 10 out (two slips); using 600,000 subscribers gives $18m, not the answer.

Raises $64,000 reverses the sign; lowers $120,000 charges the 40c premium on all 300,000 current shakes (ignores the tier and the extra volume); raises $120,000 ignores the tier and the $1.40 bar cost, so 60,000 extra shakes earn $2 each; ignoring the 20% rise gives −$100,000 and ignoring bar costs +$20,000, so no slip lands on −$64,000.

47% is a near-miss figure (45.1%, or 51 over a total that drops one bar), the profitability statement is the one statement about data not covered that sourceHas lists, and the Infusion pumps claim is a near miss where both lines are exactly $0.25m per engineer.

Threshold question on a 5kg grid: 21kg comes from leaving out the set-up times, 31kg from leaving out the hand set-up time, 36kg continues the spacing; the 365-day slip that still lands on 26kg is the one sourceHas names.

The 68% statement applies the second pie's share to all visitors (wrong base), the 55% 'only' statement over-reads 'main reason', and the money-spent statement is the single statement about data not covered that sourceHas lists.

A keeps the complement of each commission rate (1 − rate), B divides by the rates and multiplies by the hours (two reversed operations), and C adds instead of multiplying and swaps the two rates (two slips).

Twice compares the margins alone (15 ÷ 8 = 1.9), half reverses that comparison (8 ÷ 15 = 0.53), the same compares the growth rates (19% against 17%); skipping the growth step still gives three times, which is the slip sourceHas names.
50 takes the efficiency-to-fuel ratio 6:24 = 25% as the share, 30 is the blast furnace's own total, and 20 is the 20% share given as the answer, so the 10-step grid has slips behind its neighbours.
